correctness.rationale: The Gram matrix is exactly the convolution form and is positive semidefinite. A pair of distinct nonzero hyperbola parameters produces one and only one ordered parabolic collision in odd characteristic by two independent linear equations, yielding total 2(q−1)^2. Its q integer row sums have total congruent to 2 modulo q, hence the constant vector is not an eigenvector. The discrete variance lower bound 2(q−2)/q and A²≼λmax(A) A give the exact displayed gap. Exact field checks at primes 5,7,11,13,17,19 support, but are not needed for, the all-prime-power proof.

originality.rationale: The closest 2024 primary work derives single-surface convolution sharpness and constant extremizers, whereas this claim constructs a different planar mixed parabola–inverse-hyperbola Gram matrix, proves exact total collision incidence, shows its integer row sums cannot be constant, and establishes an explicit strictly positive operator norm gap for all odd finite fields. Source full text was inspected in its relevant introduction and Section 3. Search did not identify an equivalent or logically dominating earlier published mixed result; this is best-knowledge originality, with a residual synonym/indexing risk.

value.rationale: Flat inputs are natural extremizer candidates for finite-field curved-surface extension and do maximize important single-parabola inequalities in the 2024 primary reference. The result shows that transferring this intuition to the natural mixed parabola–inverse-hyperbola operator fails for EVERY odd finite field; it identifies a geometric reason (unique off-diagonal collisions), a universal nonstationarity obstruction, and an explicit positive quantitative gap. This is a structural all-field counterexample to flat mixed extremality, not a renamed finite splitting table or a bare integer divisibility observation. Its exact sharp constant is deliberately left open.
